title: acer glabrum subsp. douglasii
intro: Acer glabrum subsp. douglasii, commonly known as Douglas maple, is a subspecies of the glabrum maple tree native to North America. The Douglas maple is valued for its health benefits, particularly in traditional medicine, where it is used to treat conditions such as fever, sore throats, and coughs due to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of the Douglas maple include its ability to soothe and calm the body, acting as an expectorant to relieve congestion, and its antiseptic properties to prevent the spread of infections. The bioactive constituents of the Douglas maple include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
